newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end weak, pause after strong rise.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end weak, pause after strong rise.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended slightly lower on Tuesday, pausing for a breather after Monday's powerful rally but managing to cling onto most of the previous session's gains as investors remained optimistic on the market's outlook.
The Hang Seng index fell 26.31 points to 12,106.76, following Monday's advance of 227.56 points. Turnover was HK$7.14 billion compared to HK$8.56 billion on Monday.

"The market has run up something like 1,000 points in the last few weeks and although we remain positive for the long term ....the market probably looks a little bit overbought at these levels," said Keith Irving, head of research at HG Asia.

"We think it is likely probably to trade in a range for a few weeks before we see strength in either retail sales or a rebound in trade figures or something like that which will help to drive the market forwards," he added.
The Hang Seng index has gained 948 points since the end of August.

"If you look at the market, the property developers rose, then the (property) investors and then the laggard utilities. Everything has risen. It's a kind of liquidity driven market," said Kelvin Tang, analyst at ImPac Asset Management (HK) Ltd.
"In the short-term we expect to see a mild correction and then wait for more positive news from the property market or from the improving economy in China, " he said.
The Hang Seng hit a new 1996 intra-day high during the session at 12,179.04 points.
Irving said the blue chip index could trade between 11,800 and 12,000 points for the next few weeks.
Shares in Hang Seng Bank fell HK$1.75 to HK$84.25 and HSBC Holdings slipped HK$0.50 to HK$146.00.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong rose HK$0.25 to HK$61.00 and Henderson Land rose HK$0.25 to HK$68.25.
China Light shares also held strong, adding HK$0.70 to HK$36.50.
Shares in Pearl Oriental rose HK$0.125 to HK$3.475. The company said it would place 500 million warrants and use the proceeds to acquire a five-star hotel in Macau.

Trading in shares of Hopewell Holdings and its Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA) unit was suspended on Tuesday at the request of the companies pending annoucements, the Hong Kong stock exchange said. Hopewell shares closed at HK$4.425 on Monday and CEPA at HK$16.10.
